baseline_red.reason: Actual Git status did not reject tiny injected byte or record limits while acquisition was unbounded.

intermediate_run.reason: Descendant fixture inspected /proc immediately after SIGKILL, before delivery; replaced immediate assertion with a bounded same-PID/birth termination observation.

implemented: Only _plan_bound_git status acquisition uses bounded selectors; non-status commands retain their existing subprocess.run contract.
Capture refuses stdout beyond 67108864 bytes, stderr beyond 65536 bytes, or stdout beyond 70000 NUL records before adding excess bytes to retained buffers.
The existing sanitized Git command/environment and native 30-second deadline remain in effect; text/byte CompletedProcess behavior is preserved.

Each capture launches start_new_session=True and verifies its leader PID/session/group. Failure SIGKILL targets only that owned process group, then waits up to one second to reap the exact leader and closes all local pipes.
Owned process-group authority is cleared immediately after successful leader reaping; decoding failure cannot signal a reused group identity.
Existing recovery aggregate size/record and semantic custody checks remain in place.
qualification_scope: Actual native Git status with small byte/record caps reproduces and rejects unbounded-acquisition conditions.
Actual native Git return types and ambient GIT_DIR isolation.
Harmless authored Python subprocesses exercise stdout/stderr/record overflow and timeout, with exact owned leader reaping and closed pipes.
Actual forked child retains output pipes after leader exit; timeout fences the dedicated owned group and confirms same-birth descendant terminates within a bounded interval.
Invalid text decoding after a reaped leader raises without any process-group signal.
limitations: No live model calls or benchmark score.

A terminated orphaned descendant may remain a zombie until its actual parent or init reaps it; the helper reaps its exact Popen leader and the control verifies no same-identity descendant remains running.
